title: High School Teacher Salary: Award Rates, Casual Loading, and Super Paid on Top
description: Understand the high school teacher salary under the Educational Services Award. Learn how hourly rates convert to annual pay, casual loading, and superannuation paid on top.
salarySummary: A full-time high school teacher at Level 1 under the Educational Services (Teachers) Award earns $1,455.40 per week, or $38.30 per hour based on 38 hours, equating to an annual salary of approximately $75,941.

faqs.q: How is a high school teacher salary calculated from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply the hourly rate by 38 hours per week (the standard full-time hours under the Award) and then by 52 weeks. For example, a Level 1 teacher at $38.30 per hour gives $38.30 × 38 × 52 = $75,941 annually. This matches the Award's annual rate. Part-time teachers are paid pro-rata based on their weekly hours.

faqs.q: Does a casual high school teacher get a 25% loading on top of the base rate?
faqs.a: Yes. Under the Educational Services (Teachers) Award, casual teachers receive a 25% loading on the daily rate. For a full day at Level 1, the casual rate is $363.85 (weekly rate divided by 5 plus 25%). This loading compensates for leave entitlements not received. Superannuation is also paid on top of the casual rate.

faqs.q: How does superannuation affect a high school teacher salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (from 1 July 2026). For a full-time teacher earning $75,941, the employer contributes an additional $9,113 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is not deducted from your salary; it's an extra benefit.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the High School Teacher Salary Under the Award

If you're looking to convert an hourly rate into an annual **high school teacher salary**, the starting point is the **Educational Services (Teachers) Award 2020** [MA000077] from the Fair Work Commission. This award sets minimum wages for teachers in preschools, schools, and long day care centres. The rates are updated each 1 July. For the 2026–27 financial year, a full-time teacher at Level 1 (graduate or provisional accreditation) earns **$1,455.40 per week**, which is **$38.30 per hour** based on 38 ordinary hours. That works out to an annual salary of **$75,941** (weekly rate × 52.18, as per the Award).

### Hourly to Annual Conversion: The 38-Hour Week

The standard full-time week under the Award is 38 hours. To convert an hourly rate to annual pay, use the formula:

**Hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks = annual gross salary**

This assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a Level 1 teacher at $38.30 per hour, that's $38.30 × 38 × 52 = $75,941. The Award actually uses 52.18 weeks to calculate the annual rate, but 52 weeks gives a close estimate. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool on this site uses 52 weeks for simplicity.

For part-time teachers, the same hourly rate applies, but you multiply by your actual weekly hours. A part-time teacher working 19 hours per week at Level 1 would earn $38.30 × 19 × 52 = $37,840 annually.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation Paid on Top

Casual teachers receive a **25% loading** on the daily rate, as set out in the Award. For a full day at Level 1, the casual rate is **$363.85** (weekly rate divided by 5, plus 25%). This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. The [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to add this to your base rate.

**Superannuation** is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the Super Guarantee is **12%** of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a full-time teacher earning $75,941, the employer contributes an extra **$9,113 per year** into your super fund. This is not deducted from your salary; it's an additional benefit. The [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page has more details.

### Fortnightly Pay and Tax Considerations

Many teachers are paid fortnightly. A full-time Level 1 teacher's fortnightly gross pay is **$2,910.80** (weekly rate × 2). After tax and Medicare, the take-home amount depends on your tax bracket. For 2026–27, the tax-free threshold is $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. Medicare levy is generally 2%. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator to estimate your net pay.

### Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is **$26.44 per hour** for a 38-hour week, or **$1,004.90 per week**. The **high school teacher salary** under the Award is significantly higher, starting at $38.30 per hour. The Award also includes higher rates for experienced teachers (Levels 2–5) and for those in long day care centres (an extra 4%). For example, a Level 5 teacher (Highly Accomplished) earns **$2,013.70 per week** or **$52.99 per hour**, an annual salary of **$105,076**.

### Using the Timesheet Tool

To convert your own hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, or weekly figures, try the [timesheet](/) tool. Enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading) and check the box to add 25% casual loading if applicable. The tool will show your gross pay per period and estimate tax and super. Remember, super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings, so the total cost to your employer includes your salary plus 12% super.

### Summary of Key Points

- **Full-time high school teacher salary** under the Award starts at $75,941 per year (Level 1).
- Hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks gives a close annual estimate.
- Casual loading of 25% is added to the daily rate, not the hourly rate.
- Superannuation of 12% is paid on top of ordinary earnings.
- Fortnightly pay for Level 1 is $2,910.80 gross.
- Always check the latest Award rates from the Fair Work Ombudsman or the Fair Work Commission.

For more reference tables, see the [reference tables](/data) page. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page compares teacher salaries to national averages.

This guide provides an estimate only. Your actual pay may vary based on your classification, hours, and any applicable allowances or penalties.
